name: kbd
title: Kbd
description: Keyboard shortcuts in tooltips, menus, and command lists.
docs: ## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/kbd ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd"; export function ShortcutHint() { return ( Search ⌘K ); } ``` ## Single key Use one `Kbd` for one physical key. It is a hint, with no focus stop or keyboard handler. ```tsx import { Kbd } from "@/components/cadence/kbd"; export function EscapeHint() { return Esc; } ``` ## A combination `KbdGroup` renders the keys with one gap between them and keeps the sequence together for screen readers. ```tsx import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd"; export function CommandHint() { return ( Ctrl Shift P ); } ``` ## Inside a tooltip A `Kbd` inside `data-slot="tooltip-content"` inverts its colours automatically, so the hint stays legible on the tooltip surface. Focus or hover the trigger to see it. Install `@cadence/tooltip` and `@cadence/button` for this composition; the application owns any save action or shortcut handler. Tooltip and Button keep their own motion contracts and inherit the site's motion settings. ```tsx import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { Kbd, KbdGroup } from "@/components/cadence/kbd"; import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/cadence/tooltip"; export function SaveHint() { return ( }>Save changes Save ⌘S ); } ``` ## When to use - A shortcut hinted next to a command: search, save, new item. - A key the user should press in a flow: `Tab`, `Esc`, `↑ ↓`. - Inside a `tooltip` or a `dropdown-menu` item, where space is short. ## When not to use - A key that is part of running text. Write it in prose; a pill interrupts the sentence. - A button that runs a command. A `kbd` is a label, not a control — it has no keyboard path and no press state. - Long sequences of more than three keys. Put the shortcut in a table instead. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | ---------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | | `Kbd` | native `kbd` props | One key. `data-slot="kbd"`. | | `KbdGroup` | native `div` props | Wraps several keys with `data-slot="kbd-group"`. | KbdGroup keeps the pinned native div prop type while rendering a `kbd` element. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A key hint is a label; it must not pulse or slide while the user is reading it. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - Renders a real `` element, which assistive technology reports as keyboard input — the same information a sighted user reads from the key shape. - The shortcut is text, so it survives every reduced-motion mode and every colour theme. - If a hint is icon-only, put the key name in `aria-label` on the `Kbd`. - Do not attach `tabIndex`; a shortcut hint is not focusable. ## Responsiveness and performance Keys and key groups use intrinsic inline sizes. The caller owns wrapping or scrolling long shortcut descriptions; these labels do not register keyboard shortcuts. T0 adds no authored animation runtime or interpolation. This wrapper renders HTML/CSS; interactive children and application handlers still need their own client code. Server-rendered markup does not imply that every interaction works without JavaScript. The registry enforces a 4 KiB gzip budget for this item's own shipped source; dependencies and application bundles are measured separately. ## Notes for AI - Use the platform's own glyphs (`⌘`, `⇧`, `↵`) rather than words, and keep one `Kbd` per physical key. - If the shortcut is a live command, render a `button` and put the `Kbd` inside it.
